subject: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer

Hi Markus / Laura —

Quick note: as we finalize the Q4 hiring freeze bands, I want to request an exception to retain the Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer (IC-6) on my team. We have a planned handoff for a GreenLight Health POC next month and a live rollout dependency on the model KV-cache changes that only this engineer is fully up to speed on.

Why I'm asking for an exception now:
- Single-point failure: the role is the primary author of the KV-cache stability work and the rollout playbook. No other engineer on the team has the same operational context.
- Customer risk: GreenLight's integration (pilot) goes live 10/12 — losing this knowledge risks a rollback and a potential SLA breach.
- Ramp time: recruiting + ramp for an external hire is ~4–6 months; interim contractor support is expensive and still requires ~3 weeks of handover.

I've attached a short justification memo and the position justification doc. If we can't keep the headcount, I propose a 6-week contractor bridge (Jesse Park) while we negotiate an exception. Cost delta estimate in the memo.

Requested action: approval for a freeze exception to keep the position funded through Q1 or permission to extend a contractor for 6 weeks to cover the rollout.

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync if helpful.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Engineering Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer

Sergio —

Thanks for the write-up. A couple quick clarifying questions before I escalate:
1) Can you quantify the expected revenue / renewal impact if GreenLight experiences a rollback? Any estimate of short-term churn or contract credits?
2) What's the fully-burdened cost comparison between keeping the headcount vs. a 6-week contractor extension (include recruiting/overlap costs)?
3) Are there any feasible reassignments inside the org that mitigate the single-point risk (e.g., temporary shadow from Marcus' team)?

If you can send the numbers I can push this through the leadership freeze-exception queue today.

-MK
Markus Klein
VP, Platform Engineering

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>; Jesse Park <jesse.park@talentworks.io>
Date: 2026-09-11T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer

Markus —

Answers below, and I've attached the cost table in the memo for quick reference.

1) Revenue/risk: GreenLight's POC is directly tied to a potential enterprise contract expansion. If the pilot fails or we request a rollback, their procurement team indicated a two-week pause on negotiations and potential 10% credit request on the pilot milestone (~$45k). Longer disruption could jeopardize the Q4 expansion (estimate: ~$250k ARR ramp delay).

2) Cost comparison (rounded):
- Keep headcount (salary + benefits, prorated to Q4): $45k
- 6-week contractor + onboarding + overlap (Jesse): $28k
- Recruiting + open requisition time penalty (loss of velocity on other features): ~ $12k impact estimate
Net: contractor is cheaper short-term but does not eliminate institutional knowledge risk. Document includes scenarios.

3) Reassignment: we examined Marcus' team; they can send one senior engineer for a 2-week shadow, but that engineer lacks deep KV-cache/rollout ownership — high risk of missed edge cases.

Recommendation: Approve a short freeze exception through end of Q1 if leadership is comfortable; otherwise approve the 6-week contractor but mandate an extended pair-programming handoff and a written runbook (I'll own runbook delivery).

Next steps if approved:
- Laura: leadership approval for exception OR
- Monica: procurement guidance and quick contractor engagement if exception denied.

Thanks,
Sergio

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer

Sergio / Markus —

Process notes:
- For a headcount exception we need: role-level justification (you attached), customer impact statement (please add a one-paragraph summary we can include in the approval ticket), and the org-level mitigation plan.
- If leadership denies the exception, we can onboard Jesse as a contractor within 7 business days if you approve SOW terms (procurement will expedite).

Operational suggestion: I recommend the contractor + shadow plan as a fallback while the exception is considered. That buys us time without immediate risk to the customer and keeps the option to convert if leadership approves.

I'll prepare the approval ticket once Laura signals a direction.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. People Partner (Engineering)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: freeze exception to retain senior ML-infra Engineer

Thanks for the thoughtful packet, Sergio. I reviewed the memo and Markus' notes. Given the customer risk and the relatively small delta to keep the headcount through Q1, I approve a targeted exception for this role with two conditions:

1) Sergio to deliver the runbook + 2-week shadow plan for the contractor (if used) within 5 business days.
2) We treat the exception as conditional: we review status at the end of Q1 and re-evaluate conversion or reallocation then.

Monica, please open the leadership exception ticket and mark it as "approved pending documentation" and flag it for Q1 review. Sergio, coordinate with Procurement and Jesse (cc'd earlier) to arrange contractor terms as contingency.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference
